newsitem.title: USA: Canadian farmers seen switching back to oilseeds.
newsitem.headline: Canadian farmers seen switching back to oilseeds.

text.p: Canadian farmers will plant more oilseeds this year and less wheat than last year although fewer acres may be switched than many had been forecasting a few months ago, analysts said.
"We went into oilseeds two years ago, went out of them last year and are now going back into them," said Greg Kostal, analyst with Continental Grain Canada.
Statistics Canada is due to issue its first 1997 plantings projection, based on intentions at the end of March, on Wednesday at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT.
Kostal said his canola plantings forecast for western Canada was 12.75 million acres, up 45 percent from the prior year which StatsCan estimated at 8.802 million.
He noted, however, he had originally forecast area at 14 million acres but cut his estimate two months ago.
"The psychology has changed here," he said, noting the recent strength of wheat prices and the prospect of good wheat seeding conditions had helped to change the mood.
Kostal noted, however, that some of the mood change had taken place since late March. "You are going to get the lowest wheat forecast of the year (by StatsCan Wednesday)," he said.

LFG analyst Rob Dzisiak, said he expected canola plantings to be "somewhere around 12 million acres" citing strong oilseed prices and rotation influences as among the factors behind the switch to crops like canola and flaxseed.
He also expected oilseeds to lose some ground to wheat after the report. "I think we will see more wheat acreage in the end (than on Wednesday)," he said.

A survey by United Grain Growers issued earlier this month projected canola acreage at 12.166 million acres. The survey put all wheat area at 27.393 million, down 11 percent from StatsCan's estimate of last year's acreage at 30.725 million.
Kostal, of Continental, said he believed the StatsCan report may understate wheat acreage by about 500,000 acres and possibly overstate barley and canola area.
His forecast for all wheat area in western Canada was 28.5 million acres.
Kostal put barley area at 11.5 million acres, down from StatsCan estimate for last year of 12.4 million.
The UGG survey put barley planting intentions at 11.83 million.
The survey put oats planting intentions at 4.529 million acres, below StatsCan's estimate for last year of 4.785 million. Kostal put oats area at around 4.4 million.
"I'm looking for a small decline in all the cereals," Kostal said.

Flaxseed plantings, like canola, were seen rising on strength in world oilseed prices with the UGG survey projecting area at 2.098 million acres, up 41 percent from StatsCan's estimate for last year of 1.49 million.
Kostal said he expected flaxseed "to have a big number, in excess of two million (acres)."

Flooding in southern Manitoba was seen reducing wheat acreage in the area and increasing plantings of barley and flaxseed. However, overall the impact on western Canadian plantings, was expected to be minor.
A Canadian Wheat Board expert last week said that 500,000 acres of mainly wheat fields could be flooded by the swollen Red River.
((Chicago newsdesk 312-408 8720))
